title: Late-evidence obligation cannot be closed: resolution TP fills re-latch LATE_EVIDENCE and the audit never clears the invariant violation
requirement: NG-CELL-003 (a late fill creates a new TP obligation of the old cycle, closed by TP), NG-HIST-002 (freeze until audit), AC-08, AC-42 (ledger part), NG-CELL-001
failure_scenario: BUY cell, gen0 entry fills 4, is proven terminal (4), TP 4 fills and is proven, cycle released. A late history fill of 1 on the gen0 entry correctly returns LATE_EVIDENCE. The operator acknowledges it (acknowledge_late_evidence(0)) and a resolution TP of 1 is dispatched for gen0. When that TP fills normally, apply_fill returns LATE_EVIDENCE again and sets cycle.late_evidence=True, because `late = leg.is_final or cycle.closed` (cells.py:586) treats every fill on a released cycle as late, including fills of a TP created after the audit. Per handoff item 4, the engine freezes again, and every partial fill of the resolution TP needs another audit. acknowledge_late_evidence (cells.py:621-629) also leaves terminal_cumulative=4 with filled=5, and leaves a REJECTED_* leg with fills unchanged. So check_invariants (cells.py:681-685) reports 'gen0 ENTRY#0: filled 5 != terminal cumulative 4' (or 'rejected leg has fills') for the whole life of the ledger. Trace open-risk #4 says the engine must freeze on check_invariants(), so the market is frozen permanently after any late evidence, and no ledger API can repair it.
suggested_fix: Treat only fills on already-final legs as late (`late = leg.is_final`). In acknowledge_late_evidence, turn the audited leg into TERMINAL with terminal_cumulative = filled (including REJECTED_* legs that executed) and record that correction durably. Add a committed test for the full late-evidence -> audit -> resolution TP -> release cycle.

title: TP headroom planner declares RISK_BLOCKED when the only same-side entries are SUBMIT_UNKNOWN (could still be cancelled)
requirement: NG-RISK-002 (RISK_BLOCKED only when the cap is still incompatible after same-side pending entries are cancelled; otherwise cancel and wait for history terminal)
failure_scenario: The cap is 20 and P_max is 20 because of a same-side BUY entry of 20 in SUBMIT_UNKNOWN (for example after a restart, when mark_intents_unknown ran, or after a timeout). A BUY TP of 10 needs headroom. plan_tp_headroom counts only CANCEL_IN_FLIGHT entries as in_flight and only LIVE/INTENT entries as candidates, so SUBMIT_UNKNOWN entries count as unfreeable: freeable 0 < excess 10, so risk_blocked. The router emits BLOCKED (router.py:226-232) and the engine goes to operator-required RISK_BLOCKED, although the entry will resolve to LIVE (then cancellable) or to a zero-fill reject (then freed). The same input with the entry LIVE gives CANCEL + WAIT.
suggested_fix: Count same-side SUBMIT_UNKNOWN entry remainders as freeable-pending, like in-flight entries, and return WAIT. Return RISK_BLOCKED only when confirmed position plus non-entry orders alone exceed the cap.

title: _split_valid chunks greedily by max_base and creates DUST when an exact valid split exists
requirement: NG-GRID-003 (DUST only when the exact remainder is below the runtime minimum; no silent resize), AC-34 (runtime rule change must not create an unfillable TP when a valid one exists)
failure_scenario: Q=10 entry accepted under max_base=None, fully filled and proven terminal. Runtime rules then change to max_base=6 (min_base 5, step 1). _split_valid takes chunk=min(10, 6)=6, leaving 4 < 5, so the TP plan is (6,) with DUST 4 and the cell is locked. The exact split 5+5 is valid under the new rules. dust.aggregate (dust.py:108) behaves the same way: it skips the whole group when the total exceeds max_base instead of forming a valid aggregate at or below max_base.
suggested_fix: When chunking by max_base, choose chunk sizes so that the final remainder is 0 or >= min_valid, for example by balancing ceil(remaining/chunk_cap) equal step-multiple chunks. Mark DUST only if no such partition exists.

title: AC-39 is claimed done but tested only on a helper the ledger never uses; CellLedger cannot store an aggregate TP or its per-cell allocation
requirement: AC-39 (one aggregate TP splits partial fills exactly between cell obligations, idempotently); NG-GRID-003 (the ledger keeps each cell's allocation)
failure_scenario: Cell 3, min 5. Gen 0 was released, then late evidence adds a 2 obligation. The entry is final, so refresh_dust makes it DUST 2. Gen 1's entry ends partial and leaves DUST 3. dust.aggregate() builds a valid SELL 5 at the same target, but CellLedger.add_tp_intent(5, generation=g) raises LedgerError 'exceeds unassigned obligation': qty must be <= one cycle's unassigned (cells.py:488-490). AggregateTp.apply_fill returns per-lot deltas, but no CellLedger method applies them to cycle E/X/buckets, and to_record() has no allocation field. The cell stays locked with DUST 5 even though a valid aggregate exists. Any aggregate order WS-D placed could not be reflected in the ledger.
suggested_fix: Either add a ledger representation for aggregate TP legs (allocation per (cell, generation) persisted in to_record, fills applied through the allocation to each cycle's X) and test it end to end through CellLedger, or downgrade AC-39 in the trace to 'not implemented in ledger' with a WS-D handoff.

title: AC-34 / NG-RISK-005: no test covers rejecting full Q at the TP price after a runtime floor change; dropping that check in admission and begin_entry passes the suite
requirement: AC-34 (a new floor blocks invalid submits); NG-RISK-005 (full Q must be valid at the entry price AND the paired TP price; a cell must not be armed into certain permanent DUST)
failure_scenario: At runtime, min_notional rises to 54.8. SELL cell 26 has entry 5.4909 (10 x 5.4909 is valid) and TP 5.4727 (10 x 5.4727 < 54.8, invalid). The current code correctly blocks it with FULL_Q_INVALID_TP. But if admission._full_q_blocker or CellLedger.begin_entry checked only the entry price, every test still passes. The cell would be armed, fill 10, and its TP of 10 would be BELOW_MIN_NOTIONAL, leaving the cell in permanent DUST.
suggested_fix: Add runtime tests where a floor makes full Q invalid only at the TP price of a SELL cell, e.g. min_notional=54.8 with cell 26. Assert admission.plan blocks it with FULL_Q_INVALID_TP and CellLedger.begin_entry raises.

title: AC-57 no-starvation claim unproven: replacing head-of-line queueing with skip-ahead passes the suite
requirement: AC-57 (no starvation; queued cells advance deterministically); NG-RISK-005 (queue by distance, then cell_id)
failure_scenario: Mutation: in plan(), let later idle cells arm when the head cell does not fit (replace 'head_blocked = True' with 'pass'). The whole suite passes, because every sample cell needs exactly 3 slots, so head-of-line and skip-ahead behave the same. With a floor that makes some TP prices need 4 slots (e.g. min_notional=27, step 0.01: TP 5.5 gives min_valid 4.91, so 4 slots; TP 5.4 gives 5, so 3 slots) and 3 free slots, skip-ahead arms 3-slot cells ahead of the queue head every tick. The head starves indefinitely, and no test detects it.
suggested_fix: Add an admission test with different required_slots per cell, where the head needs more slots than are free. Assert that nothing behind it is newly_armed and that it arms first once the slots free up.

title: CidAllocator does not latch on a malformed durable lookup, although its docstring says it does
requirement: NG-HIST-004 / AC-43 (fail closed on invalid, colliding or overflowing CIDs; the handoff says 'a latched CidError must drive the engine to DEGRADED')
failure_scenario: The durable map returns 2**48 for identity A (a corrupt row). allocate(A) raises CidInvalid, but allocator.failed stays None, and allocate(B) then succeeds and mints CID 1. An engine that relies on the latched 'failed' flag to go DEGRADED keeps submitting with a corrupt CID map. The module docstring (line 8) says a 'malformed value latches the allocator'. The test at test_cid.py:70-71 asserts only the raise, not the latch.
suggested_fix: Route validate_cid failures from lookup through self._fail(...), and assert alloc.failed is set and later allocations raise.

title: When the venue/user order cap drops, the router still sends TPs from stale per-cell reservations and goes over the cap
requirement: NG-RISK-005 (effective max_active_orders/venue cap; slots are never counted twice); NG-RISK-002 (emergency entry cancel is meant for an unexpected venue cap reduction); AC-44; the spec §13.3 property that caps are never violated
failure_scenario:
1. One BUY cell is armed with cap=3 and reserves 3 slots. Its entry is live (actual=1).
2. The venue cap drops to 1, so rules.max_active_orders_venue=1.
3. The entry partially fills 5 of 10.
4. admission.plan reports SlotLedger(cap=1, actual=1, reserved_unused=2, free=-2), which is oversubscribed.
5. SlotBudget.from_plan still gives the cell cell_unused=2, and the router returns SUBMIT 'tp:10:0:0' with reason 'OK'.
6. There are now 2 resting orders (the 5-lot entry remainder plus the 5-lot TP) against an effective cap of 1.
7. The AC-44 emergency path (select_entries_to_cancel) never runs, because budget.take never returns None.
8. The venue then rejects the TP for too many orders. That can loop into a new revision on every tick, or the order goes over the user's configured cap.
suggested_fix: When plan.slots.free < 0, remove the oversubscription from the unused reservations: cut idle and entry reservations first and exit reservations last, or have SlotBudget.from_plan take the deficit off cell_unused. A TP that cannot fit inside eff_cap then takes the emergency-cancel path: cancel a cap-consuming LIVE entry, wait for history terminal, then submit.

title: NOT_SENT / DEFINITIVE_REJECT_ZERO_FILL releases a leg whose CID already possibly or provably reached the venue
requirement: NG-DB-005, NG-HIST-004, AC-56 (also AC-16/AC-17: UNKNOWN keeps reservation, no new CID)
failure_scenario: (a) First submit returns UNKNOWN (timeout), so the order may be resting on the venue. The engine re-dispatches the same CID with mark_dispatching(resend_same_cid=True), and the second call hits connector pre-send validation (NOT_SENT) or a venue 'duplicate client id' reject (DEFINITIVE_REJECT_ZERO_FILL). record_transport_result moves the leg to REJECTED_UNSENT/REJECTED_ZERO_FILL, releases the reservation, cycle_release_blockers returns [], and _check_single_physical_entry accepts a new ENTRY revision with a new CID. Result: a possibly live first order is no longer tracked or reserved, and duplicate exposure follows. (b) An active-orders poll records the order (record_order_evidence, then set_leg_state LIVE) before the transport result is written. A later NOT_SENT still makes the leg REJECTED_UNSENT and releases its reservation.
suggested_fix: Accept NOT_SENT/DEFINITIVE_REJECT only for a row's first dispatch (attempts == 1, with no earlier UNKNOWN outcome). Refuse them, or record a durable conflict, when the leg is past SUBMIT_UNKNOWN or has venue evidence (last_evidence_ms, exchange_order_id, ACCEPTED). In every other case keep SUBMIT_UNKNOWN and the reservation.

title: mark_dispatching silently re-authorises transport for an already DISPATCHED (unknown-outcome) row without resend_same_cid, even when degraded
requirement: NG-HIST-004 (same-ID repeat only with documented venue idempotence, otherwise UNKNOWN), NG-DB-002 (Unknown does not lead to blind retry), AC-16, AC-55
failure_scenario: The process dies after transport was called but before the result committed, leaving the outbox row DISPATCHED. On restart the engine walks unresolved_outbox() and calls mark_dispatching(tx, id) the same way it does for PENDING rows. For the DISPATCHED row the call succeeds, returns status DISPATCHED and leaves attempts at 1, so under the protocol the engine is cleared to call transport and sends the same CID again without the explicit resend flag. The durable attempts counter under-counts the real sends. The early return also comes before the degraded check, so a degraded store still authorises this SUBMIT.
suggested_fix: Treat a DISPATCHED row like DONE/UNKNOWN: refuse re-dispatch unless resend_same_cid=True, increment attempts, and apply the degraded check first. If in-process idempotence is needed, key it on a per-process dispatch token rather than on status alone.

title: Default paths put both prior-run markers inside the same data directory as the DB, so wiping it yields a fresh bootstrap, reused CIDs and a newly adopted baseline
requirement: AC-54, NG-DB-004 (missing DB with prior-run evidence is not created clean and does not take the current position as B), NG-HIST-004/AC-43 (unique CID)
failure_scenario: Deployment with the documented defaults (path None, lock_dir None) and no prior_run_markers callback, which is optional and defaults to None. The operator loses or deletes <data>/neutral_grid, which holds the DB, <db>.marker.json and locks/<key>.marker.json. NeutralGridStore.open(..., create_if_missing=True) finds no evidence and creates a fresh DB with cid_epoch 1. bootstrap() accepts a new B as a first bootstrap, and the first allocated CID equals the lost DB's first CID.
suggested_fix: Put the host marker in a location independent of the DB data directory by default, or make a venue-evidence prior_run_markers callback mandatory whenever create_if_missing=True. Also consider deriving the fresh-DB epoch from venue-observed CIDs.

title: Late fill after cycle release creates an obligation that can never be covered by a TP and disappears from the restart view
requirement: NG-HIST-002 (late evidence after reuse belongs to the old cycle), NG-CELL-003 (late fill creates a TP obligation of the old cycle), NG-DB-003 step 6 (restart restores TP obligations), AC-42/AC-52
failure_scenario: Entry of 10 fills 6, is canceled and proven TERMINAL; TP 6 fills and the cycle is closed COMPLETE. A late 2-LIT trade on the old entry is then applied to the COMPLETE cycle (E=8, X=6) with LATE_FILL and CUMULATIVE conflicts. After the operator audit, allocate_cid and record_intent both refuse a TP for the closed cycle ('cycle ... is not open'). load_state().open_cycles omits it, so a restarted engine never sees the obligation. grid_mutation_blockers() returns [] even while the LATE_FILL conflict is unresolved, so migrate_grid proceeds despite its docstring. The 2-LIT obligation is orphaned.
suggested_fix: Let a late fill on a COMPLETE cycle reopen it or mark it as having an outstanding obligation that allows TP allocation after audit. Include cycles with entry_filled != exit_filled or late_evidence != 0 in load_state, and include them plus unresolved conflicts in grid_mutation_blockers.

title: The same-host single-writer lock sits under the per-checkout data_path, so two checkouts can run two engines on one account and market
requirement: NG-DB-001
failure_scenario: default_lock_dir() is <data_path()>/neutral_grid/locks, and hummingbot.data_path() is <checkout root>/data. The same host has two checkouts or worktrees, or two containers with their own data volumes. Each launches the engine for the same account and market. Each takes its own flock on a different lock file and opens its own DB, so both engines trade the same account. Both DBs start at cid_epoch 1, so their CIDs also collide.
suggested_fix: Put the account+market lock in a fixed host-wide location that does not depend on data_path (for example ~/.hummingbot/neutral_grid/locks or /var/tmp). Change the test to open two stores with different data paths and the default lock_dir.

title: Prior-run 'host marker' is inside the data dir: wiping data/neutral_grid makes a fresh DB, a new baseline and reused CIDs
failure_scenario: In the default layout the DB is data/neutral_grid/<key>.sqlite3 and the host marker is data/neutral_grid/locks/<key>.marker.json. The operator deletes data/neutral_grid (or data/) after the DB is lost. The next open(create_if_missing=True) finds no evidence and creates a fresh database with cid_epoch 1. The operator bootstraps a new B, and the first new entry gets the same CID (1<<40|1) as the previous engine's order that may still be live.
suggested_fix: Keep the host marker outside data_path (the same host-wide location as the lock) and add a test that uses default_db_path/default_lock_dir with a shared base_dir.

title: migrate_grid ignores obligations on COMPLETE cycles (late fills) and open history conflicts; the 'obligations' test covers only a live order
requirement: AC-52, NG-ARCH-003
failure_scenario: The entry is partially filled 4 and proven TERMINAL, the TP of 4 is filled and TERMINAL, and the cycle is closed as COMPLETE. A late fill of 1 on the entry arrives: it is applied, the cycle becomes E=5 and X=4, and LATE_FILL plus CUMULATIVE_EXCEEDS_ORDER conflicts open. grid_mutation_blockers() returns [] and migrate_grid() succeeds. The old grid is RETIRED with an unhedged obligation of 1 that can never get a TP, because record_intent requires an OPEN cycle.
suggested_fix: Block migration for any cycle (OPEN or COMPLETE) of the old grid with entry_filled != exit_filled, late_evidence==1, open history conflicts or unallocated fills. Add a late-fill test.

title: The retention-gap entry block lives only in the manual_reconcile flag: an unrelated reconciliation clears it, and gaps written through cursors never block
requirement: AC-53, NG-DB-004
failure_scenario: (a) mark_retention_gap(TRADES) sets manual_reconcile_required. Later the operator resolves an unrelated PAYLOAD_MISMATCH conflict with record_manual_reconciliation(resolved_conflict_ids=[id], evidence about trade size). The default clear_manual_reconcile=True lifts the gap block while cursors.TRADES still says complete=0 'retention gap'. entry_blockers()==[] and new entries are accepted without any reconciliation of the gap. (b) The engine persists CursorUpdate(required_boundary_ts_ms < oldest_available_ts_ms, complete=True) through apply_history_batch or update_cursors. The store accepts it and never blocks entries.
suggested_fix: Derive a blocker from cursor state (required_boundary_ts_ms < oldest_available_ts_ms, or a retention-gap incomplete_reason). Refuse complete=True while a gap is recorded. Clear the gap only through a reconciliation that names the stream/gap, not as a side effect of resolving other conflicts.

title: NOT_SENT is accepted for an already-DISPATCHED/resent submit: the leg is finalised, its reservation is freed and a new ENTRY CID is allowed after a timeout
requirement: NG-HIST-004 (no new ID after timeout/crash), NG-DB-005, AC-56, AC-17
failure_scenario: The entry submit times out, so the store records UNKNOWN and the leg is SUBMIT_UNKNOWN with its reservation held. The engine then calls mark_dispatching(resend_same_cid=True), which clears outcome to NULL and sets attempts=2. On the resend, the port's local pre-validation fails (for example the runtime minimum changed) and returns NOT_SENT. record_transport_result maps this to REJECTED_UNSENT, a final state, and releases the reservation. _check_single_physical_entry then allows ENTRY revision 1 with a new CID. The first attempt may still be live or filled on the venue, so exposure is doubled under a new CID. If the first attempt then fills, _apply_trade reports it as EVIDENCE_FOR_UNDISPATCHED_INTENT and the fill is never credited. The same happens after a restart: a DISPATCHED row left by the dead process accepts NOT_SENT.
suggested_fix: Accept NOT_SENT only for a PENDING row, or for a DISPATCHED row dispatched by this same process/owner token with attempts == 1 and no earlier outcome. On a resend, record NOT_SENT as the result of that attempt only and keep the leg SUBMIT_UNKNOWN with its reservation.

title: A late fill on a released (COMPLETE) cycle raises E, but no TP can ever be recorded for it, and the cell can re-arm after the audit
requirement: NG-CELL-003 (late fill creates a TP obligation of the old cycle), NG-CELL-001, NG-HIST-002, AC-08, AC-42
failure_scenario: The entry partially fills 4 of 10 and is canceled; TERMINAL is proven. A TP of 4 fills and the cycle is closed as COMPLETE. A delayed history fill of 1 then arrives: _apply_trade credits it to the old cycle (E=5, X=4) and raises LATE_FILL. Every attempt to cover it fails: allocate_cid and record_intent raise 'cycle ... is not open' (the same holds for allocations). After the operator resolves the LATE_FILL conflict, entry_blockers is empty and open_cycle starts generation 2 of the same cell, because the previous cycle is still COMPLETE. The 1-unit obligation is stranded with no TP. grid_mutation_blockers also ignores it, since it checks only OPEN cycles.
suggested_fix: When a late fill leaves E != X on a COMPLETE cycle, reopen it or mark it as having an open late obligation. Allow TP intents and allocations for that obligation, and make open_cycle and grid_mutation_blockers refuse while any cycle of the cell has E != X.

title: Aggregated TP allocations are not checked for the same side and fixed target price, so fills can close another cell's obligation at the wrong price or on the wrong side
requirement: AC-33/AC-39 (aggregate only by same side + target), NG-CELL-002, handoff: do not move fixed targets
failure_scenario: record_intent for a TP of BUY cell 5 (SELL @5.109) is given allocations=[(grid,5,1,10),(grid,40,1,10)]. Cell 40 is a SELL-entry cell whose fixed TP is BUY @5.7272. The store accepts it. When the aggregated SELL fills, allocate_fill credits cycle 40's exit_filled with a SELL execution, so the store sees E==X and allows the cycle to be released and re-armed. The venue short from cell 40 was actually doubled, not closed. Allocating to a cell with a different TP price in the same way closes that cell's obligation away from its fixed target.
suggested_fix: In _insert_allocations, require every target cycle to have tp_side == the request side and tp_price == the request price, and require the leg role to be TP.

title: A final aggregated TP with unallocated fills drops out of the TP-headroom invariant, so a duplicate TP is admitted
requirement: NG-CELL-002 invariant confirmed_exit + reserved_TP_unfilled <= confirmed_entry; status lag must not create a duplicate TP (NG-CELL-002, AC-39, AC-51)
failure_scenario: A TP leg of 10 with an allocation to cycle 5 fills 10 in history. Allocation is deferred (the split policy is WS-A's), then the final order row arrives and set_leg_state(TERMINAL) passes. It checks only venue cumulative == leg.filled and releases the reservation. _tp_reserved now skips the leg because it is final, and X was never credited, so X + reserved = 0 while 10 has already been sold. prepare_submit for TP revision 1 with 10 is accepted, which is a duplicate TP of the full obligation.
suggested_fix: In _tp_reserved, count the unallocated fill quantity of allocated TP legs regardless of leg state, or refuse TERMINAL for a leg with allocations while any of its fills is unallocated.

title: Store guards raise after partial writes and do not poison the transaction, so a caller that catches InvalidTransitionError (as the handoff instructs) commits half-applied state
requirement: AC-55 / NG-DB-002 (nothing half-applied), NG-HIST-002 atomic ledger transitions, AC-39
failure_scenario: Handoff item 7 tells WS-D to catch EntryBlockedError/InvalidTransitionError and show them as blockers. Inside the history tx, allocate_fill(key, [(5,2),(6,6)]) inserts the part for cycle 5 and credits X5=2, then raises for cycle 6 ('exceeds 5'). The caller catches it and the tx commits. Result: an 8-unit fill is only 2-allocated, and unallocated_fills() and verify_ledger() both report nothing wrong. The correct allocation is then refused forever ('already allocated differently'), leaving cycle 6's executed exit uncredited. Similarly, record_intent with allocations summing 9 != 10 inserts leg/orders/outbox/reservation/allocations before raising ValueError; if that is caught, a PENDING dispatchable SUBMIT with inconsistent allocations commits.
suggested_fix: Validate everything before the first write (the sum, per-part caps, cycle state), and/or mark tx._failed whenever a store method raises after it has written, so a swallowed guard error cannot commit.

title: record_order_evidence(final=True) lets a non-history (WS/active-list) row become the terminal proof that releases the reservation
requirement: NG-HIST-001/NG-HIST-002 (WS, cancel events and active-list disappearance are not terminal proof; terminal release needs the exact history terminal row), handoff forbidden compromises
failure_scenario: The engine passes a WS 'canceled' event, normalised as an ExchangeOrderRow, to record_order_evidence(tx, row, final=True). This sets orders.venue_final=1 without any history_inbox row, dedupe key or payload-conflict check. set_leg_state(TERMINAL) then passes the store's 'exact final venue order row' check and releases the reservation, and the cycle can be closed. A late history fill is then treated as late and the cell may already have re-armed.
suggested_fix: Remove the `final` parameter (the active-orders path must never set venue_final), or set venue_final only from INACTIVE_ORDERS rows applied through apply_history_batch/inbox.

title: A CUMULATIVE_EXCEEDS_ORDER conflict key is reused, so a further excess fill after the operator resolved the first conflict is silently not re-flagged
requirement: AC-40 (trade cumulative > order cumulative stops exposure), NG-HIST-002 (conflict -> pause)
failure_scenario: The terminal order row says filled=3 and trades sum to 4, which raises CUMULATIVE_EXCEEDS_ORDER. The operator resolves it. A new trade of 2 for the same CID arrives (leg not final, so no LATE_FILL): leg.filled=6 against venue 3. _check_cumulative builds the same key 'CUMULATIVE_EXCEEDS_ORDER:{latest inactive inbox id}:{cid}', INSERT OR IGNORE does nothing, and the returned record is the already-resolved one. No open conflict exists and entry_blockers is empty while the ledger holds 3 more units than the venue order cumulative.
suggested_fix: Include the offending quantity (leg.filled) or the triggering trade inbox id in the key, or re-open/insert a new conflict when the matching conflict is already resolved.

title: An ENTRY intent may carry allocations across several cycles, so the store accepts physically glued entries
requirement: NG-CELL-002 (one physical entry per cycle; entries must not be glued)
failure_scenario: record_intent(entry_leg(3), amount 20, allocations=[(g,3,1,10),(g,4,1,10)]) is accepted. The fills are later split with allocate_fill into cycle 4's entry_filled even though cycle 4 has no own entry leg. The one-physical-entry guard (_check_single_physical_entry) sees only cycle 3, so cycle 4 can also get its own ENTRY and hold two physical entries worth of E.
suggested_fix: Reject allocations when role == ENTRY.

title: Conflicting duplicate key inside one scan still emits the first-seen payload as a new row, so a guessed quantity gets committed
requirement: AC-40 (duplicate ID with different size stops exposure, quantity is not guessed); NG-HIST-002 (one key with different payload = conflict and pause)
failure_scenario: In one walk, trade key K arrives on page 1 with size=1 and again on page 2 with size=2 (or an inactive order row arrives with filled=3 and then filled=5). _apply_row keeps the first version in progress.rows (line 639) and only records a conflict for the second. _result (lines 470-474) returns every uncommitted row, so new_trades still holds K with size=1 even though the result has complete=False and reason=conflict. The documented engine contract (trace: 'new_trades/new_orders are rows not yet committed; committing them is idempotent by key') and the reference InMemoryHistoryCursorView.commit (lines 247-264, 'mirrors the engine's atomic commit') commit new rows whatever result.complete says. The size=1 payload therefore becomes the committed fill and the ledger applies a quantity the venue contradicted. On later scans the size=2 version is flagged as committed_payload_mismatch against that arbitrary first pick.
suggested_fix: Track conflicted keys per stream and exclude them from new_trades/new_orders; the whole key goes to manual audit. Or document and enforce that no row from a result that carries conflicts may be committed.

title: Order dedupe key includes the client id, so one exchange order index with contradictory client id and fill amounts passes as a complete scan
requirement: AC-40 (duplicate ID with different payload is a history conflict); NG-HIST-002 (one key with different payload => conflict; canonical keys over exact exchange ids)
failure_scenario: The venue serves inactive-order rows for the same order_index X twice: once with client_order_index=1002 and filled=3, and once with client_order_index=999 and filled=5. That is a venue inconsistency, or a row whose client id is reported differently across scans. order_dedupe_key returns (domain, account, market, exchange_id, client_id), which gives two distinct keys. No duplicate or payload mismatch is detected, and the scan returns complete=True with two contradictory terminal rows for one exchange order. The engine may then settle CID 1002 against filled=3, and a later scan that serves X with a different client id is committed as a new order instead of raising a conflict. order_payload_fingerprint also compares client_order_id/client_order_id_str, but because those fields are part of the key, that comparison can never fire.
suggested_fix: Key inactive-order rows by (domain, account, market, exact order_index/order_id) only, and keep the client id in the payload fingerprint so that a disagreement becomes a conflict. Alternatively, add an explicit exchange-id uniqueness check across keys within a scan and against committed rows.

title: The CID-order polling exclusion lives only in memory: after a restart, restored grid orders go back to legacy per-order polling, recentTrades polling and lost-order auto-cancel
requirement: NG-HIST-003 (weights 600/100/300, 18000/min pool, no request storm, exhaustion must not starve proof); WS-C decision 'CID orders excluded from per-order polls'; NG-DB-002 (no cancel without durable intent)
failure_scenario: _history_reconciled_client_order_ids is an in-memory set (line 113), filled only by submit_with_client_id (line 1589). Hummingbot saves tracking_states (all updatable orders, including CID orders) and restores them on every strategy start (trading_core.py:538 -> markets_recorder.restore_market_states -> ClientOrderTracker.restore_tracking_states). Take a restart with about 60 live grid orders. The overridden _update_orders (line 306) and _update_trade_history (line 421) now see those orders as legacy ones. Every status poll calls _request_order_status -> _find_order for each order: accountActiveOrders at weight 300, plus inactive at weight 100 when the order is not active. That is 60 x 300 = 18000, the whole Standard per-minute pool, in every poll cycle, plus recentTrades at 600. The authoritative HistoryScanner is queued behind this in the shared throttler and cannot finish, so the engine stays RECONCILING (NG-DB-003) and cannot release cells. On top of that, the base _handle_update_error_for_active_order counts any polling exception as not-found. After 3 errors a live grid order becomes lost, and _lost_orders_update_polling_loop -> _cancel_lost_orders -> _place_cancel -> _find_order can send a cancel tx for a grid order that has no engine outbox intent.
suggested_fix: Make the exclusion survive a restart: override restore_tracking_states (or tracking_states) so that CID-submitted orders are tagged (for example in misc/marker state) and re-added to the exclusion set on restore, or are not restored into the legacy tracker at all. Also exclude them from the lost-order escalation and cancel path.

title: release_history_reconciled_order says the CID stays refused, but the refusal expires with the 30 s tracker cache, and release briefly re-enables recentTrades polling
requirement: NG-HIST-004 / AC-56 (after timeout or crash a new send of the same CID is allowed only with documented venue idempotence; outcome stays UNKNOWN)
failure_scenario: The docstring promises 'the order stays in the tracker cache, so the same client id is still refused by submit_with_client_id'. stop_tracking_order moves the order into ClientOrderTracker._cached_orders, a TTLCache with CACHED_ORDER_TTL = 30 s. After 30 s fetch_order (line 1575) no longer finds it, and a replayed outbox dispatch of that CID reaches create_order and puts a second order with the same client_order_index on the venue, whose duplicate-CID behaviour is undocumented. The same happens 30 s after a WS terminal event, which also calls stop_tracking_order. In addition, release discards the CID from _history_reconciled_client_order_ids while the order sits in the cache, so _update_trade_history counts it as fillable again. That triggers weight-600 recentTrades polls for up to 30 s after every release, which the design says CID orders must not cause.
suggested_fix: Keep a durable or process-lifetime set of CIDs ever sent through submit_with_client_id and refuse them regardless of the tracker cache (or correct the docstring so WS-D does not rely on it). Keep released CIDs excluded from _update_trade_history.

title: Conflict results still return the conflicted key's first-seen payload as a new trade, and the reference commit stores it
requirement: AC-40 / NG-HIST-002 (same key with a different payload means conflict and pause; the quantity is not guessed)
failure_scenario: A trades page returns the same dedupe key twice, once with size 2 and once with size 7. The scan reports complete=False with conflict duplicate_key_payload_mismatch, but result.new_trades still contains the first-seen size-2 row. InMemoryHistoryCursorView.commit (history.py:247-264) commits new rows whether or not the result is complete, and it is documented as mirroring the engine's atomic commit. It stores size 2 as the committed fill, so the ledger takes an arbitrarily chosen quantity for a conflicted key. The trades that exceed a terminal order's cumulative fill (the AC-40 cumulative conflict) are likewise returned in new_trades.
suggested_fix: Exclude every key involved in a conflict (and the rows of an order in a cumulative conflict) from new_trades/new_orders, or state in the contract and in InMemoryHistoryCursorView.commit that rows are committed only when complete. Then add assertions to the conflicting_duplicate and AC-40 tests that the conflicted key is absent from new_trades.

title: The AC-56 'never retry with a new CID' tripwire is swallowed by the connector's broad except and becomes the expected UNKNOWN
requirement: AC-56 / NG-HIST-004 (timeout or not-found stays UNKNOWN and does not create a new CID)
failure_scenario: Suppose submit_with_client_id regressed to retry after a failed send with self._new_client_order_id() inside the try block at lighter_perpetual_derivative.py:1607-1614. The mocked tripwire raises AssertionError, and 'except Exception' at line 1613 turns it into UNKNOWN 'transport_exception: AssertionError'. That is exactly the outcome test_ac56_timeout_not_found_and_errors_are_unknown_and_never_retry_with_new_cid expects. create_order is still awaited once with the original CID, so the test passes.
suggested_fix: After each subtest, assert self.connector._new_client_order_id.assert_not_called() and the exact detail prefix (for example 'transport_exception: TimeoutError' or 'transport_error: ...').

title: CID orders restored after a restart fall back to legacy per-order polling and lost-order handling, which starves the authoritative history scanner
requirement: NG-HIST-003 (CID orders must not be polled per order, the pool must stay available for the scanner, bounded restart work under the throttler); NG-DB-003 (restart reconciliation); NG-DB-002 (no cancel without a durable intent)
failure_scenario: 1) The engine has about 55 live CID orders (entries and TPs), some possibly SUBMIT_UNKNOWN (PENDING_CREATE). 2) Hummingbot's MarketsRecorder persisted them via tracking_states when their OrderCreated/Fill events fired. 3) The process restarts. TradingCore restore_market_states() puts them back into in_flight_orders, but _history_reconciled_client_order_ids is an in-memory set that starts empty. 4) The overridden _update_orders and _update_trade_history no longer exclude these orders. Each status cycle (LONG_POLL_INTERVAL=60 s) runs _find_order per order: accountActiveOrders at 300 weight, plus accountInactiveOrders at 100 if the order is not active. That is about 16,500 of the 18,000/min Standard pool, spent during restart RECONCILING, exactly when the paginated trades (600) and inactive-orders (100) scans must run. 5) Restored UNKNOWN orders that are not found become 'lost' after more than 3 polls. _lost_orders_update_polling_loop then runs _cancel_lost_orders every 5 s, costing 400 weight per attempt. If such an order is later indexed by the venue, _place_cancel sends a cancel tx for an engine order with no outbox intent. The trace's own weight analysis says this polling 'would exhaust the 18000/min pool and starve the authoritative scanner'.
suggested_fix: Make the exclusion survive a restore. Options: override restore_tracking_states and tracking_states so that CID-path orders are either not persisted or are re-marked on restore (for example, from a durable marker or an InFlightOrder attribute). Alternatively, require the engine to call a register_history_reconciled_order(cid) for every durable CID before the polling loops start. In either case, keep CID orders out of lost-order auto-cancel. Add a restart test that covers restore_tracking_states.

title: Hummingbot stop/exit cancels every CID order through the legacy cancel path, bypassing the engine's durable cancel intent and stop-uncertainty handling
requirement: NG-DB-002 (every submit/cancel needs a durable intent first); NG-OPS-003 and the handoff's forbidden compromise 'не объявляй stop успешным при uncertain cancel'
failure_scenario: 1) The operator types `stop` or `exit` in the Hummingbot CLI running the neutral-grid launcher. 2) With the default skip_order_cancellation=False, stop_command.py:39-40 calls trading_core.cancel_outstanding_orders(), which calls connector.cancel_all() for every connector with limit_orders. 3) submit_with_client_id registered every CID order via start_tracking_order, so cancel_all iterates all live engine entries and TPs. It calls the legacy _place_cancel, which finds the order with a one-page _find_order (include_inactive=True) and sends signer.cancel_order. 4) No CANCEL_PENDING or outbox intent is written to the engine ledger, and none of the cancel_with_client_id classification runs. The tracker marks the orders PENDING_CANCEL locally. Hummingbot completes the stop regardless of cancel outcome, so the engine's STOPPING/STOP_UNCERTAIN logic never runs. On restart, the engine finds TPs canceled that it never asked to cancel.
suggested_fix: Exclude history-reconciled CID orders from the generic cancel_all/limit_orders path, for example by overriding cancel_all to skip ids in the CID set, so that engine orders are cancelled only via cancel_with_client_id after a durable intent. Alternatively, document and enforce that the launcher stops with skip_order_cancellation. Add a test showing that cancel_all sends no cancel tx for CID orders.

title: The port's trading_rules() always reports limit and post-only as supported and ignores the venue's force_reduce_only market state
requirement: NG-GRID-003 (availability of limit orders comes from fresh trading rules); NG-RISK-004 (unknown or blocked market state blocks new exposure)
failure_scenario: 1) The venue sets market_config.force_reduce_only=true on the LIT market, for example during a wind-down. The market stays status=active and not hidden, so is_exchange_information_valid still accepts it. 2) LighterExchangePort.trading_rules() returns supports_limit=True and supports_post_only=True. 3) The engine keeps admitting and dispatching reduce_only=false entries and TPs. 4) The venue rejects them. The sendTx error is classified UNKNOWN, so reservations and slots are held with no history row ever appearing. Alternatively the orders end as canceled-reduce-only. Cells stay stuck in SUBMIT_UNKNOWN until a manual audit, instead of new exposure being blocked up front. The legacy snapshot already treats this state as non-tradable.
suggested_fix: Derive supports_limit and supports_post_only (or raise HistorySchemaError) from market.raw_info status, hidden and force_reduce_only after _update_trading_rules(). Report the market as not tradable when force_reduce_only is true or the fields are missing.

title: confirm_baseline can start the engine without Start, the risk acknowledgement or a preview check
requirement: NG-UI-002 (first live start needs a separate explicit confirmation of expected_initial_position and of risk), NG-UI-003 / AC-47 (Start semantics)
failure_scenario: The engine is AWAITING_START, which is the web-driven start path used by the generic controller without the launcher phrase, or the demo. Once bootstrap.ready is true, the operator clicks the always-visible «Подтвердить baseline» button (index.html:72) and types B before ever sending Start. _validate returns early for every non-START kind (lines 235-239), so it never checks engine_started, risk_acknowledged, preview_id or preview errors. The engine's _cmd_confirm_baseline (engine.py:797-839) bootstraps the grid and sets meta.started=True. It also skips the config.enabled gate that START has (engine.py:723). The grid then starts placing orders without the Start dialog's risk confirmation or the preview validation.
suggested_fix: In _validate, refuse confirm_baseline with 409 unless views.engine_started(snapshot) is True, meaning a Start carrying risk_acknowledged and preview_id was applied. Hide or disable the button until then. On the engine side (WS-D), _cmd_confirm_baseline should require meta.started, and the enabled/offline_demo gate as START does.

title: Attach mode cannot load the shipped controller config (missing account_index), and any separate grid.yml can drift from the engine
requirement: NG-UI-001 / NG-ARCH-001 (the UI reads the single engine's committed state), NG-UI-002 (preview/baseline correctness), integration with WS-D controller config
failure_scenario: An operator follows the README and runs `--attach-db <engine.sqlite> --config conf/controllers/lighter_robinhood_fixed_neutral_grid.yml`, the only grid config the branch ships. grid_config_from_mapping calls GridConfig(**kwargs), which requires account_index; the controller YAML lacks it because the account comes from the connector at runtime. The web process crashes with a TypeError. The only workaround is a second, hand-written GridConfig YAML. The web then takes the preview, the Start/confirm B check (config_baseline) and preview_id from that file, not from the engine's config. If the two drift (for example the controller has B=330 and grid.yml has B=0), the preview shows the wrong reachable range ([-330,+220] instead of [0,+550]) and the web rejects the correct B with 422.
suggested_fix: Load the controller config format (NeutralGridConfig) and read account_index and the grid config from the store's committed engine/grid record (bootstrap config), or refuse to start when the file disagrees with the engine record's fingerprint and baseline.

title: The UI never shows a persistence failure: the banner needs a snapshot that cannot be committed, so the UI only shows STALE while CLI status shows the error
requirement: NG-DB-004 / AC-55 (the UI shows the persistence failure), §11 (CLI status and UI show the same state)
failure_scenario: The disk fills or the database becomes read-only. Engine.tick catches PersistenceError and never commits a snapshot while the store is degraded (engine.py:612-616, 625-627). So summary.persistence_error is never present in a committed snapshot and the persistence banner never appears. The web shows the last state (for example NORMAL) as current for up to stale_after_s, then «Нет свежих данных». The demo host holds the engine in-process, but host.status() does not expose engine.persistence_error, and the UI does not render `host`. The CLI status (executor.py:304 local_error) does print «LOCAL ERROR (not committed): SQLITE_FULL».
suggested_fix: In the in-process host, add engine.persistence_error and fatal_reason to host.status() and render them as the persistence banner, marked as not committed. In attach mode, have the engine write an out-of-band marker file, or show «persistence unknown» next to STALE.

title: Attach-mode preview hard-codes post-only/limit support and has no freshness gate on rules and mid taken from the snapshot
requirement: NG-UI-002 (preview shows runtime floors and validation errors before start), NG-GRID-003 / NG-RISK-004 (fresh trading rules)
failure_scenario: The engine's snapshot runtime_rules has no supports_limit or supports_post_only fields (snapshot.py:161-166), and snapshot_market rebuilds TradingRules with supports_limit=True and supports_post_only=True. Scenario: the Lighter port reports post-only as unsupported. The engine's validate_config rejects LIMIT_MAKER at confirm_baseline (CONFIG_INVALID). The attach preview meanwhile shows errors=[] and can_start=true, and the web accepts the Start. Second scenario: the attached engine died hours ago. Rules and mid come from its old snapshot with no staleness check, the preview presents them as current, and a Start is queued that nothing will apply.
suggested_fix: Have the engine snapshot publish supports_limit and supports_post_only, and use them (unknown should block). In attach mode, add a preview error when the snapshot or its rules are older than history_freshness_s or stale_after_s.

title: ID lookup and audit paging silently scan only the newest 5000 rows and report «found 0» for older IDs
requirement: NG-UI-002 (drill-down by order/trade IDs and audit history), AC-22 (IDs pass API/UI pagination and matching)
failure_scenario: A long-running 55-cell grid accumulates more than 5000 fills or legs. An operator looks up the trade_id_str or exchange order id of an older fill. find_trades and find_orders search only fills()[-5000:] and legs()[-5000:], so the API returns empty lists and the UI prints «найдено 0», claiming absence. Similarly, commands and audit paging with `before` fetch only the newest 5000 rows, so after about 100 pages next_cursor leads to an empty page and older audit history cannot be reached.
suggested_fix: Use indexed store queries (by exchange_order_id / trade_id_str, and `id < ?` for commands and audit), or at least return a `truncated` flag that the UI shows instead of «найдено 0».

title: Engine error timestamps reach the UI as strings and always render as «—»
requirement: NG-UI-002 (summary shows recent errors), §11 parity
failure_scenario: The engine records errors with a float `at` (engine.py:664). The store writes it as a JSON float, and _loads(parse_float=Decimal) returns it as a Decimal. for_display converts only str time values, so jsonsafe emits `at` as a string. app.js fmtTime(e.at) returns «—» for anything that is not a number, so every entry under «Последние ошибки» has no time. snapshot.committed_at in /api/state is also a string. The web test covers only engine-shaped string times, which the real store never returns for errors.
suggested_fix: In for_display, also convert Decimal values under DISPLAY_TIME_KEYS to float, and add a test built from a real store snapshot.

title: Workstream gate fails: browser truth/security/keyboard test races a 5 s staleness window against cold Chrome start
requirement: AC-48 / AC-49 / AC-50 (browser proof claimed DONE in trace/ws-e-web.md)
failure_scenario: The fixture snapshot is built with committed_at=time.time() (ngweb_fakes.py:46), and the test sets stale_after_s=5. The snapshot is never refreshed before line 55 waits for 'Работает'. The failure comes from how the test is written, not the product. If Chrome launch plus navigate plus login takes more than 5 s, the UI correctly shows STALE ('Нет свежих данных'), 'Работает' can never appear, and wait_for times out. test_ngweb_browser.py sorts first in the directory, so it gets the cold Chrome start.
suggested_fix: Set web.gateway.snapshot['committed_at']=time.time() after _open(), or inject a controllable ctx.clock. Another option is a large stale_after_s for the first half of the test that only drops for the STALE step.

title: AC-50 history-lag assertions pass even without injecting history lag (normal polling already produces ~5.75 s lag)
requirement: AC-50 (history lag in the offline fake-exchange flow), NG-UI-002 (history lag visible)
failure_scenario: If the 'history_lag_on' demo action were a no-op, or the engine ignored history lag, both tests would still pass. On the real demo engine, the normal WS-signal-to-history delay with fake lag 1 s and 5 s poll coalescing already pushes summary.history.lag_s to about 5.75 s. That clears the API test's `lag_s > 3` threshold and the browser test's `/^[1-9][0-9]* с/` (≥1 s) regex at test_ngweb_browser.py:221-222. The 'nothing credited without history' check at line 191 samples `during` as soon as lag > 3 s. That is before the normal ~5.75 s crediting, so it passes without any injected lag.
suggested_fix: Assert a lag above the no-injection ceiling, e.g. ≥10 s while fake.history_lag_s=30. Keep the entry's filled unchanged across that longer window, then assert it is credited after history_lag_off. Apply the same threshold to the browser check.

title: Attach mode: Start preview and risk/baseline confirmation come from a separate --config YAML and are never checked against the config the engine actually runs
requirement: NG-UI-002 (first live start needs a separate explicit confirmation of B and risk, based on a preview of the real grid); NG-UI-001 (versioned committed snapshot); NG-UI-003 (Start returns the existing engine identity)
failure_scenario: The engine runs in the Hummingbot executor from the controller YAML with Q=20 and caps 2000. The web is started with --attach-db and a stale or different grid.yml (Q=10, caps 1000, other grid_id). /api/preview shows P_min/P_max [-330,+220], gross 550/1000 and no errors. The operator types B and ticks the risk box, and POST start returns 202. The engine applies START without looking at preview_id or B (engine.py:722-734). CONFIRM_BASELINE only compares B, so the engine then trades a grid with twice the exposure the operator confirmed. /api/state and the 409 engine_already_running responses also report the web YAML's grid_id instead of the engine's. Reproduced with a scratch script: snapshot summary had grid_id=engine-real-grid, order_amount_base=20 and caps 2000. The preview showed Q=10, cap 1000, errors []. Start returned 202, and identity came back as {'grid_id': 'web-yaml-grid'}.
suggested_fix: In attach mode, build the preview from, or at least validate it against, the engine's committed config in the snapshot summary (or a config fingerprint the engine publishes). Refuse to start the server, or return 409/422 on Start, when grid_id/connector/pair/bounds/N/Q/caps/leverage/B differ. Take engine_identity from the snapshot.

title: Attach mode cannot load the shipped controller config, and silently drops or defaults any config keys it does not recognise
requirement: Integration with final core/store/controller (NG-ARCH-001/003: one config for the engine and the preview; the preview must show the configured profile); AC-46
failure_scenario: The operator follows the README: `--attach-db <db> --config conf/controllers/lighter_robinhood_fixed_neutral_grid.yml`, the only grid config the branch ships. The controller config has no account_index, because the connector resolves it at runtime. grid_config_from_mapping then calls GridConfig(**kwargs), which raises TypeError: 'missing 1 required positional argument: account_index', and the launcher dies with a traceback (reproduced with load_grid_config on the .example file). To use attach mode the operator must hand-write a second YAML. Any key that is misspelled, missing or named differently there is silently skipped (runtime.py:69-70) or replaced by a GridConfig default, e.g. history_freshness_s or tp_gtt_seconds. The preview then shows values the engine does not use, which is the divergence behind the previous finding.
suggested_fix: Load the preview config from the engine's committed snapshot or bootstrap record, or parse the NeutralGridConfig controller YAML through the controller's own pydantic model with account_index taken from the store identity. Reject unknown or missing keys instead of silently defaulting them.

title: Store lookups and pagination silently stop at the newest 5000 rows, and the UI reports 'found 0' or end-of-history
requirement: NG-UI-002 (drill-down by order/trade IDs and audit history); AC-22 (trade/exchange IDs pass API/UI pagination and matching); handoff: no silent truncation
failure_scenario: After a few weeks of 55 cells cycling (entries, partial TPs and GTT renewals), the ledger holds more than 5000 legs or fills. The operator looks up the exchange order id or trade id of an older disputed fill. find_orders scans only legs()[-5000:], and find_trades scans only fills()[-5000:]. The response has orders: [] and trades: [] with no truncation marker, and the UI prints 'найдено 0'. The operator concludes the trade is not in the ledger. Likewise, audit and commands paging fetch only the newest 5000 rows and filter by id < before. Once the cursor passes that window, the next page is short and next_cursor is None, so the journal looks complete while older audit events cannot be reached.
suggested_fix: Use indexed store queries (by exchange_order_id, trade_id_str, and id < ? LIMIT ?) instead of windowed Python scans. If a bound is kept, return an explicit `truncated: true` / `scanned_up_to` and show it in the UI rather than 0 results or end of list.

title: Attach-mode preview hard-codes LIMIT/post-only support as available and labels the snapshot time as the rules fetch time
requirement: NG-GRID-003 (limit-order availability comes from fresh runtime trading rules); AC-46 (validation shown before start); NG-RISK-004 (rules freshness)
failure_scenario: The Lighter market leaves the tradable state. lighter_port.py:322-323 then sets supports_limit=supports_post_only=False, and the engine's validate_config reports 'venue does not support post-only LIMIT_MAKER'. The snapshot's runtime_rules do not carry these flags, and snapshot_market always passes True. The attach preview therefore shows no validation error, can_start=true, and enables Start. The engine only refuses later, at CONFIRM_BASELINE. The preview's rules_fetched_at is also the snapshot commit time (runtime.py:128), not rr['fetched_at'], so rules that are hours old are shown as fresh.
suggested_fix: Publish supports_limit/supports_post_only in the snapshot's runtime_rules (a WS-D change) and pass them through. If they are absent, treat the rules as unknown (preview error) instead of assuming True. Show the real rules fetched_at and flag rules as stale when they are older than the engine's max rules age.

title: TP-dispatch SLO clock is frozen at tick start and anchored to the first fill: real multi-second delays show as 0.0 s, and an immediate dispatch shows as a 60 s breach. The AC-14 test cannot fail.
requirement: NG-CELL-002 (durable TP intent reaches the router <=2 s after the history-fill commit; blockers show queue age and exact reason), AC-14, NG-RISK-002 (TP priority over entries)
failure_scenario: (a) 12 BUY cells fill in one tick and each submit/cancel round trip takes 0.4 s. The engine awaits every transport in turn (_submit -> _dispatch_intent at 1864). The 12th TP intent is committed about 4.4 s after the history commit, but tp_latencies records 0.0 and the snapshot shows last/max_latency_s = 0.0. (b) The price spikes above the upper bound while 18 SELL entries fill. _act awaits all 12 OUTSIDE_BOUNDS entry cancels first (1705) and only then commits TP intents (1707+). The first TP intent is committed at +4.8 s and the last at +11.6 s, yet all are recorded as 0.0 latency: entry housekeeping delays exits. (c) AC-05 flow: a fill of 2 at t0 stays below minimum. Then +3 arrives at t0+60 s and TP 5 goes out in that same tick. The snapshot reports last_latency_s = 60.0, a false SLO breach, because the obligation clock kept the first below-minimum fill time.
suggested_fix: Stamp the history commit and each TP intent commit with self.clock() at the moment they happen, not the tick-start now. Start the SLO clock when the obligation becomes dispatchable (the commit of the fill that clears the minimum/blocker). Commit all router-approved TP intents before awaiting any transport, and dispatch TPs before entry cancels. In AC-14, drive a clock that advances during transport.

title: A history conflict or ledger-invariant freeze on one cell withholds every cell's TP obligations and skips the outside-bounds entry cancels
requirement: NG-OPS-001 (pause keeps servicing confirmed TP obligations; a fill gap or unknown blocks only new exposure of the affected cell), NG-HIST-002 (a key with a different payload -> history conflict and pause), NG-RISK-003 (does not abandon TP obligations), NG-OPS-002 (entries are cancel-requested outside bounds)
failure_scenario: The venue serves one contradictory trade row for cell A (an overfill on A's CID). The store opens an OVERFILL conflict, tp_blockers becomes ['HISTORY_CONFLICT'] and _act returns early. Cell B is unrelated: its entry fully fills, history is complete and exact, E = 10, and venue net is +10. B still gets no TP for 60 s, and none until an operator runs ack_history_conflict. When the book then leaves the range, no OUTSIDE_BOUNDS cancel is sent: 0 cancels, 9 entries stay live. Any StoreError or LedgerError raised anywhere in a tick behaves the same way, for example an active-orders row that contradicts a leg, because it latches FREEZE_INVARIANT, which is in _FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP.
suggested_fix: Scope TP blocking to the cells/CIDs named by the conflict or invariant. Keep dispatching TPs of unaffected cells whose history is exact. Keep sending risk-reducing entry cancels (outside bounds, TP priority) while frozen. Block only new entries globally.

title: A drift check compares a position read taken before the same tick's history scan and raises a false 'position drift' RISK_BLOCKED
requirement: NG-RISK-002/NG-RISK-003 (drift detection against the durable ledger), NG-CELL-001(5) (position and ledger reconciled), NG-OPS-001
failure_scenario: B = 25 with a long cap of 30, so no BUY entry fits and 5 SELL entries rest (reachable interval [-25, 25]). A SELL entry fills 10 after the tick's account read but before its trades page is read, which is normal because REST reads are not atomic. The history commit makes P = 15 and P_max = 15, while the position read from moments earlier says 25. The engine marks manual_reconcile_required ('position drift: venue 25 outside ledger reachable [-25, 15]'). The engine goes RISK_BLOCKED and entries freeze until an operator baseline audit, even though venue and ledger both equal 15. This occurs whenever resting opposite-side remainder is below the fill quantity: near a cap, at a grid edge, or after outside-bounds cancels leave only one-sided TPs.
suggested_fix: Compare only a position fetched after the latest history commit, using real read timestamps (self.clock() at read time) rather than tick-start. Alternatively require the out-of-interval condition to persist across a fresh position read plus a complete scan before marking drift.

title: A failing trading-rules refresh is retried every tick with no backoff, eats the weight budget and starves history scans, delaying TPs
requirement: NG-HIST-003 (configurable weight limit and backoff with safe defaults; one engine, coalesced polling, no polling storm), AC-04, NG-CELL-002 (prompt TP after history)
failure_scenario: Once rules are older than rules_refresh_s (60 s), a persistent failure of order_book_details (5xx, or 'market absent' raised by LighterExchangePort.trading_rules) makes the engine charge 300 weight and retry on every 1 s tick. In 120 s the engine made 54 rules calls and only 2 history scans (control run without the failure: 24 scans). History went stale, and a fully filled entry got its TP after 41 s instead of 1 s. Steady state already uses about 15,400 of the 16,200/min engine budget, so any un-backed-off retry starves scans and account polls.
suggested_fix: Record the attempt time on failure too, and back off exponentially (as the scanner does). Charge the rules refresh against a separate or lower-priority share so history scans and account polls keep their cadence.

title: After a runtime minimum decrease, ordinary partial fills make the router emergency-cancel other cells' resting entries for slots
requirement: NG-RISK-002 (emergency entry cancel only for an unexpected venue order-cap drop or a hard-risk conflict, not to free slots that should be reserved; a regular partial fill is no reason to cancel an entry), NG-RISK-005 / AC-57 (no regular entry cancels or cancel spam), AC-34
failure_scenario: 10 cells are armed with 3 slots each under cap 30 (floor 5). The venue lowers min_base/min_notional to 1; the cap is unchanged. Cell 3's entry then receives ordinary 1-lot partial fills. Each fill is split into its own TP at the new floor (TP 1, TP 1). The third TP needs a 4th slot, so the router cancels cell 9's resting entry ('SLOT_EMERGENCY_TP_PRIORITY:tp:3:1:0'). Every further small fill on any armed cell can cancel another cell's entry.
suggested_fix: When a cell's reservation is short because rules changed (not because the venue cap dropped), keep its extra obligation undispatched inside its reserved slots. For example, accumulate while the entry is live and dispatch in chunks no smaller than the arming-time minimum, and show it as a blocker. Reserve emergency entry cancels for an actual cap reduction or a hard-risk conflict.

title: Rejected intents are re-issued with a new CID/revision every tick, with no backoff and no visible blocker
requirement: NG-DB-005 (a new revision is allowed after config/rules are fixed), AC-34 (an unfulfillable TP becomes a visible blocker), AC-56, NG-HIST-004 (CID per revision)
failure_scenario: (a) The venue changes tick size so the fixed TP price 5.4 is off-tick. Each tick the engine allocates a new CID, commits a durable TP intent plus reservation, and immediately marks it REJECTED_UNSENT (PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK): 32 dead TP legs for one obligation in 32 s, about 86k/day per obligation. The cell shows TP_REQUIRED with blocker None. (b) The venue persistently and definitively rejects one cell's entry with zero fill. The engine sends a new revision to the venue every tick: 61 submits and 61 CIDs in 60 s, while the engine reports NORMAL and the cell shows SETTLING with no blocker. Across 55 cells this is up to max_submits_per_tick=20 sends per second.
suggested_fix: Latch a per-cell blocker with the rejection reason (for example PRESEND:PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK or VENUE_REJECT:<detail>) and do not create a new revision until trading rules or config actually change (compare fingerprints), or at least apply exponential backoff. Also check that grid prices are on the current tick in admission and TP planning.

title: A WS trade signal arriving after its row is already committed creates a permanent phantom history lag
requirement: AC-13 (lag visible in status; history lag measured separately from the WS event), NG-HIST-001, AC-09 (reordered events)
failure_scenario: A fill's trade row is committed by a scan first. Later the private-stream or connector fill event for the same trade arrives (reorder, reconnect replay, or connector REST-driven OrderFilledEvent). wake() adds ws_pending[trade_id] = now, and nothing ever pops it. After 120 s with history complete, summary.history.lag_s reads 119.0 and keeps growing, so the operator sees a false history lag indefinitely. The AC-09 test's own wake({'type':'trade','trade_id':'999'}) leaves such a phantom entry.
suggested_fix: In wake(), skip labels whose trade key/CID is already in the committed cache. Also expire ws_pending entries once a complete scan whose window covers the signal time has committed.

title: A RISK_BLOCKED TP gets no per-cell blocker, and only the first blocked TP's reason (without its cell) is kept
requirement: NG-CELL-002 / AC-14 (with a blocker, status/UI shows queue age and the exact reason), NG-RISK-002 (RISK_BLOCKED requires an operator)
failure_scenario: Two TP obligations cannot fit the net cap even after all same-side entries are freed, so the router returns BLOCKED for both. The snapshot shows blocker None for both cells. summary.freezes holds only the first reason, e.g. 'RISK_BLOCKED:BUY TP 10 needs 5, entries free 0', with no cell or key. The operator cannot tell which obligations are blocked or why.
suggested_fix: Also set cell_blockers[cell] = action.reason for BLOCKED actions. Keep the freeze detail keyed by TP key/cell, for example a dict of all currently blocked obligations.

title: NG-CELL-001 release condition (5) (account position == ledger) is not proven by any engine test
requirement: NG-CELL-001 condition (5); trace row NG-CELL-001 claims test_ac01_normal_buy_cycle_rearms_buy and test_invariants_hold_under_random_fill_cancel_restart_orderings
failure_scenario: A cycle finishes (entry and TP fully filled) while the account endpoint reports venue net 3 and the ledger has P = 0. That mismatch is inside [P_min, P_max] and within the 30 s gap grace, so no drift freeze fires. If `_settle` stopped passing `self.position_reconciled` (for example `can_release(True)`), the engine would close cycle 1 and arm a full-Q generation-2 entry while position and ledger disagree. No engine test would fail.
suggested_fix: Add an engine test: complete a cycle, then keep the venue position off the ledger P (inside the reachable interval). Assert the cell stays at its generation with no new entry until the position agrees, then releases.

title: Honest-state restart test never observes RECONCILING; two assertions are tautologies
requirement: NG-HIST-003 (startup/restart stays RECONCILING between ticks); NG-UI-002 (no optimistic NORMAL); trace row NG-UI-002 claims test_status_states_are_honest_during_bootstrap_and_reconcile
failure_scenario: An engine that reported NORMAL on the first tick after a restart, before position, active orders and history were reconciled, would pass. The only 'not NORMAL' check runs before any tick, and the test just waits for NORMAL.
suggested_fix: After a restart that has a history backlog (more pages than one bounded scanner step), tick once and assert state == RECONCILING with no submits, then assert NORMAL only after a complete scan. Remove the `hasattr` tautology.

title: A cancel that was committed but never sent is never sent during a STOP drain, so the order stays live after stop
requirement: NG-OPS-003 / AC-36 (stop cancels own active orders), NG-DB-002/003 (a PENDING outbox row proves the request was never sent and must be resumed after restart)
failure_scenario: During a STOP drain the process dies, or mark_dispatching raises PersistenceError, after record_cancel_intent commits (leg CANCEL_PENDING, CANCEL outbox PENDING) and before mark_dispatching. After restart meta.stop_requested_ms is still set, so _act takes the stop branch. That branch picks only legs in CANCELLABLE={LIVE} or with _cancel_retry_due (CANCEL_UNKNOWN only), then returns without calling _resume_pending_intents. That method (lines 1919-1922) is the only code that dispatches PENDING cancel rows. The leg stays CANCEL_PENDING forever, and _reconcile_active never changes it (it is seen active and is not SUBMIT/TERMINAL_UNKNOWN). The order keeps resting on the venue and can fill after the stop (new exposure after stop). The engine sits in STOP_UNCERTAIN indefinitely, and the launcher detaches after 90 s. The tp_blockers branch (1654-1661) has the same gap: e.g. while FROZEN, a PENDING OUTSIDE_BOUNDS or router cancel is never sent.
suggested_fix: In the stop and tp-blocked branches, also dispatch legs in CANCEL_PENDING whose CANCEL outbox row is PENDING, reusing the loop in _resume_pending_intents (record_cancel_intent returns the open row; mark_dispatching then works without resend).

title: resolve_unknown_submit treats a missing or stale active-orders list as proof the submit never landed, which allows a duplicate TP with a new CID
requirement: NG-HIST-001 (absence from the active list is not proof), NG-HIST-004 / NG-DB-005 / AC-17 / AC-56 (UNKNOWN until evidence; no new CID), NG-CELL-002 (an unknown TP keeps its reservation; no duplicate TP)
failure_scenario: A TP submit times out but actually lands (leg SUBMIT_UNKNOWN). The active-orders fetch then fails, so _refresh_account sets active_rows=None (line 1088). Alternatively the account poll is skipped by the weight budget (1074-1076), which keeps rows fetched before the submit. history_complete is still True, and the gate does not check freshness. The operator or web UI sends baseline_audit action=resolve_unknown_submit. The gate `any(r.client_order_id == cid for r in (self.active_rows or []))` finds nothing, so the leg becomes REJECTED_ZERO_FILL. The obligation is then dispatched again with a new CID while the first TP still rests: two SELL TPs of 10 for an obligation of 10, and the net position can overshoot.
suggested_fix: Reject the audit unless active_rows is not None, active_at is later than the leg's dispatch time and within history_freshness_s, and a complete scan started after the dispatch (not _history_stale(now)).

title: _finish_stop ignores the baseline and an unknown position, so it declares STOPPED while the account still holds inventory
requirement: NG-OPS-003 / AC-35 (STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY; no success claimed under uncertainty), NG-RISK-001 (the baseline B is held inventory)
failure_scenario: The grid is bootstrapped with B=330. After STOP the process restarts while the account endpoint is failing, so self.position is None. Every owned order settles as terminal from history and every cycle has E==X. The inventory check only looks at cycle E/X/dust and at `self.position is not None and net_base != 0`, so the outcome becomes STOPPED. The venue actually holds 330 LIT. The executor then closes (is_stopped), and the launcher drain reports a clean stop.
suggested_fix: Count effective_baseline != 0 as inventory. Require a fresh known position before any STOPPED/STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY outcome; otherwise stay STOPPING, or STOP_UNCERTAIN after the timeout.

title: Every steady-state history walk re-reads all history since the oldest LIVE order, so history goes stale and entries are blocked
requirement: NG-HIST-003 (steady state scans only new pages down to the durable overlap boundary; must not read the whole history every 10 s; exhaustion must not become the normal state), AC-04 (no polling storm)
failure_scenario: oldest_unresolved_ms() takes the minimum intent_ms over all non_final_legs, including long-resting LIVE entries. The scanner boundary is min(high_water, oldest_unresolved) - overlap (history.py _begin). Far cells' entries rest from bootstrap for days, so every walk pages through the entire account trade and inactive-order history since bootstrap. Walk cost grows linearly with trading activity. Under the 16,200/min budget and 10 s freshness, history_stale soon becomes frequent: new entries are blocked, the engine is DEGRADED, and settlements slow down.
suggested_fix: Feed the scanner an unresolved lookback only for legs that can have old-dated missing evidence (SUBMIT_UNKNOWN, TERMINAL_UNKNOWN, CANCEL_*, or a terminal row pending). Proven-LIVE orders produce new-dated trade rows and a terminal row that the overlap from the high-water covers. Alternatively bound per-order lookups instead of full walks.

title: Active rows fetched before the same tick's history commit are recorded as evidence, aborting ticks until the next poll and delaying TP dispatch
requirement: NG-CELL-002 / AC-14 (TP intent reaches the router within 2 s of the history commit), NG-HIST-001 (the active list is acceptance evidence only)
failure_scenario: The tick fetches active_orders in _refresh_account and then runs _scan_history. If an order completes between those two reads, _apply_history commits its terminal row (venue_final, status filled). _reconcile_active then calls record_order_evidence with the older open row (filled amount changed, so the cache misses). The store raises InvalidTransitionError ('final order row changed' / 'cumulative filled regressed'). The tick aborts before _act, and _reload clears _active_reconciled_at, so every following tick re-applies the same stale rows and aborts again until the next account poll (poll_interval_s=5). No TP is dispatched in that window; the engine reports FROZEN and logs STORE_REFUSED each tick.
suggested_fix: Do not record active-list evidence for a CID whose terminal row was committed after active_at (or which is in terminal_rows / has venue_final), or re-read the active list after the history batch. Treat such a stale row as ignorable rather than a store conflict.

title: The LEDGER_INVARIANT freeze set on a store or ledger refusal is dropped by the next tick's reload
requirement: NG-OPS-001 / NG-RISK-004 (unknown or invariant-violating state blocks exposure until audited); trace decision 2 says mismatches surface as LEDGER_INVARIANT freezes that are cleared only by ack_history_conflict (line 1009)
failure_scenario: tick() catches StoreError or LedgerError, sets meta.freezes[LEDGER_INVARIANT] only in memory and sets reload_needed. The tick aborted before _commit_snapshot, so engine_meta is never persisted. At the start of the next tick _reload() → _load() re-reads engine_meta from engine_kv, and the freeze disappears. The engine returns to NORMAL with no operator ack; the only trace is the in-memory errors deque.
suggested_fix: Persist the freeze in its own transaction in the except handler (or after the reload), or re-apply it after _reload so that it is cleared only by ack_history_conflict.

title: Cells are released using the previous tick's position_reconciled flag, computed before this tick's history commit
requirement: NG-CELL-001 (5): account position and ledger must be reconciled at release time
failure_scenario: The tick order is _scan_history → _reconcile_active → _settle → _detect_drift. _settle calls can_release(self.position_reconciled) with the value computed last tick. Suppose this tick's history batch commits an unmatched manual trade (a new store entry blocker) or fills that change P. A cell whose TP settlement completes in the same tick is still released as 'NG-CELL-001 release proven'. _detect_drift then sets position_reconciled=False only afterwards (1440-1443, 1458).
suggested_fix: Recompute reconciliation (position_at >= last_history_commit_at, venue == P, no store blockers) inside _settle before releasing, or run the drift check before _settle.

title: Executor STOP is silently lost when its command row becomes CONFLICT, and it is never re-sent
requirement: NG-OPS-003, AC-35, AC-36, NG-UI-003 (Stop follows NG-OPS-003, honest outcome)
failure_scenario: The operator clicks Pause in the web UI, or any other command is applied, or the engine state changes (set_engine_state bumps engine_revision) while a tick is suspended on an await. Then Hummingbot `stop` runs: the launcher's on_stop calls drain_neutral_executors, which calls executor.early_stop(). That enqueues STOP with the revision current at that moment. At the next tick, claim_next_command turns the STOP into CONFLICT/stale_at_apply. early_stop has already set _stop_command_sent=True and never checks or re-enqueues; re-enqueueing with the same pid key returns the same CONFLICT row. The engine keeps running (PAUSED/NORMAL) and never cancels its orders. After 90 s the drain calls executor.stop(), which closes the store. The connector's cancel_all skips the engine-owned CIDs, so every owned order stays live on the venue. meta.stop_requested_ms is None, so no STOP_UNCERTAIN is recorded, and the log line wrongly claims 'durable state (STOP_UNCERTAIN) will be reconciled on the next start'. On restart the engine resumes normal trading.
suggested_fix: Track the STOP command row. If it is CONFLICT/REJECTED, re-enqueue it with fresh revisions and a new key, or make STOP revision-exempt in the engine (safety commands should not be subject to stale-preview conflicts). Only set _stop_command_sent once the row is APPLIED. Have the drain check the durable stop_requested_ms before claiming STOP_UNCERTAIN.

title: Crash between cancel-intent commit and dispatch during STOP: the durable cancel is never dispatched, and the order stays live forever
requirement: NG-DB-002 (a crash leaves a durable recovery question that restart must pursue), NG-DB-003, NG-OPS-003, AC-36
failure_scenario: STOP is applied and the engine commits record_cancel_intent for a LIVE order (the leg becomes CANCEL_PENDING, the outbox CANCEL row is PENDING). The process dies before mark_dispatching. After restart, stop_requested_ms is still set, so _act takes the stop branch. That branch only cancels LIVE legs and CANCEL_UNKNOWN legs that are due for a retry, and returns before _resume_pending_intents, the only code that dispatches a PENDING cancel row. The CANCEL_PENDING leg is never cancelled at the venue. It stays resting and can still fill, and the engine sits in STOP_UNCERTAIN indefinitely.
suggested_fix: In the stop branch (and in the tp_blockers branch), also dispatch legs in CANCEL_PENDING that have a PENDING CANCEL outbox row, for example by calling the cancel part of _resume_pending_intents before building the STOP cancels.

title: Runtime tick change makes a new CID, intent and leg every tick with no visible blocker (entry and TP churn)
requirement: AC-34 / NG-RISK-005 (changed runtime rules re-validate admission and restrict new entries; an infeasible TP becomes a visible blocker), NG-GRID-003 (tick from fresh rules), §11/NG-UI-002 blocker visibility
failure_scenario: The venue's tick coarsens (e.g. 0.0001 to 0.001), so fixed prices such as 5.3818 are no longer tick multiples. Admission and _idle_eligibility do not check the price tick, so a released cell is armed. _submit commits open_cycle + allocate_cid + record_intent, then _dispatch_intent's _pre_send_blocker returns PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK and records NOT_SENT. The cycle becomes _retry_only and the next tick issues a new revision with a new CID, repeating forever (up to max_submits_per_tick per tick). A cell whose TP price is off-tick does the same with a new TP CID per tick. The engine reports NORMAL with empty reasons and cell blocker None, and transport_detail is not set on this path. The ledger grows without bound and the operator sees no reason.
suggested_fix: Validate entry and TP prices against the current tick in admission/_idle_eligibility and in TP planning. Treat an off-tick fixed price as a durable, visible cell blocker (no intent, no CID) instead of discovering it after the intent commit. Latch the pre-send reason as the cell blocker.

title: LEDGER_INVARIANT freeze is not durable: it is wiped by _reload on the next tick, and the FROZEN state is never committed
requirement: NG-DB-003 step 7 (stay paused on any ambiguity), NG-UI-002 / §11 honest committed state
