failure_scenario: Any StoreError or LedgerError inside a tick (a store/ledger projection mismatch, such as close_cycle refused by B while A says can_release, or a refused leg transition) sets meta.freezes['LEDGER_INVARIANT'] only in memory, plus reload_needed=True, and skips _commit_snapshot. On the next tick _reload() calls _load(), which replaces self.meta from the committed engine_meta. The freeze disappears and the engine evaluates NORMAL and dispatches entries again without any operator ack, even though ack_history_conflict exists specifically to clear FREEZE_INVARIANT. If the error recurs every tick, no snapshot is ever committed, so UI and CLI keep showing the last (possibly NORMAL) committed state.
suggested_fix: Persist the freeze (kv_set engine_meta) in a fresh transaction in the except path, or merge in-memory freezes into the reloaded meta. Also commit a degraded/frozen snapshot, or at least set_engine_state, so the committed state reflects it.

title: STOP outcome ignores ledger inventory when the venue position is unknown: STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY flips to STOPPED
requirement: NG-OPS-003 / AC-35 (honest STOPPED vs STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY), NG-RISK-001 (baseline is ledger inventory)
failure_scenario: Signed baseline B=30, all cycles closed, STOP drained, outcome STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY. The process restarts while the position endpoint is failing, so self.position stays None. _finish_stop recomputes inventory from cycle E!=X or dust only, ignores the ledger net P = B + fills, and durably records and audits STOPPED ('no inventory') although the account still holds 30 LIT. The executor then closes as a clean stop.
suggested_fix: Derive inventory from the ledger (endpoints.P != 0 or effective_baseline != 0, open obligations, dust). Do not decide between STOPPED and STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY while the position is unknown or stale; keep STOPPING or report STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY.

title: No engine or launcher path to a new grid after all obligations are closed: config change is refused forever, and a new grid DB is refused as prior-run evidence
requirement: NG-ARCH-003 (a new grid is allowed after all owned orders and obligations are closed, or via an audited migration that preserves old cycles), AC-52
failure_scenario: A grid is stopped cleanly (STOPPED, store.grid_mutation_blockers() == []). The operator changes the dimensions for the next grid. With the same DB, open_engine gets ConfigMutationError ('use migrate_grid()'), but no engine command or launcher path ever calls store.migrate_grid, so the engine stays DEGRADED forever. With a new grid_id, the controller's default DB path is per grid_id (neutral_grid_<grid_id>.sqlite), while the store's host marker is keyed by domain/account/pair. The new DB is refused with PriorRunEvidenceError. A new grid on the same account/market is impossible without manual DB/marker surgery.
suggested_fix: Add an audited 'migrate_grid' operator command, or a launcher path that opens the store without the new fingerprint, verifies grid_mutation_blockers() is empty, and calls store.migrate_grid in one audited transaction. Alternatively, make the controller's default DB path per account/market (matching the store identity) so the migration path is the only route.

title: Baseline audit rebases on a position read that may predate the last committed history batch
requirement: NG-RISK-003 / AC-30 (the audit must not change obligations or mask fills); NG-RISK-001 (baseline exactness)
failure_scenario: Account poll at t=100 (every 5 s). A LIVE entry fills 10 at t=101. A WS wake causes a scan that commits the fill at t=102, so ledger buys include +10. The operator's baseline audit is applied at t=103 with observed_position equal to position(t=100). new_baseline = venue - buys + sells understates B by 10, and the rebase is persisted in the audit trail. The next poll shows venue != P, so drift or POSITION_UNRECONCILED blocks again and another audit is required. The audit mis-rebases a known fill instead of refusing a stale comparison.
suggested_fix: Reject the audit (retryable) unless position_at >= last_history_commit_at, i.e. the position read is at least as new as the last committed history batch.

title: CLI status omits the cursor progress required by operator status §11
requirement: §11 Operator status (freshness/history lag/cursor progress; per cell entry/TP requested/filled/remaining)
failure_scenario: During a long RECONCILING walk after restart, the operator runs `status`. The CLI shows only complete/reason/lag/last_full_scan/weight. The committed snapshot contains history.trades_cursor, orders_cursor, pages_read and progress (scanner.progress_summary), but none of it is rendered, so cursor progress is invisible in the CLI. TP children also show only filled/requested, without remaining.
suggested_fix: Render the trades/orders cursor (high-water), pages_read and progress in format_status, and add TP remaining per child.

title: operator_confirmed_start/baseline can be set from YAML, bypassing the launcher's confirmation phrase and Robinhood profile caps
requirement: NG-ARCH-003 (live start impossible without the change and an explicit confirmation), NG-UI-002 (first live start requires a separate explicit confirmation of B and risk)
failure_scenario: A controller YAML with enabled: true, operator_confirmed_start: true and operator_confirmed_baseline: true, run through the generic scripts/v2_with_controllers.py rather than the fixed launcher, creates the executor. It auto-enqueues START and auto-confirms B as soon as the engine is bootstrap-ready. The explicit confirmation phrase, validate_profile (leverage 5, caps <= 1000 LIT) and the 80-hex API key validation are all skipped.
suggested_fix: Exclude these fields from config loading (a model_validator rejecting True from input, or private attrs set only by the launcher), so only the fixed launcher can set them after the phrase check.

title: AC-12: no engine test shows that entries are actually held back while history is incomplete, and the store (WS-B) does not block them either
requirement: AC-12 (repeated/malformed cursor or missing page makes history incomplete; entries blocked); NG-HIST-002; NG-RISK-004; focus item 'engine blocks entries on incomplete history'
failure_scenario: Suppose a later change stops _act (engine.py:1639-1718) from honouring the HISTORY_INCOMPLETE / HISTORY_COMPLETE:FALSE / HISTORY_STALE entry blockers. Offline probe: bootstrap, push the book outside the bounds so every entry is cancelled and settled, inject a repeating trades page_error, then bring the book back inside. The mutated engine sends 10 new post-only entries while history_complete=False. The store refuses none of them, because an incomplete cursor is not a store entry blocker. The same probe on the unmodified code sends 0.
suggested_fix: Build the AC-12 scenario with at least one idle, eligible cell, for example an out-of-bounds drain and return, or a queued cell that a slot frees. Inject the page fault and assert that no ENTRY submit reaches the fake while history_complete is False, then that entries resume after recovery.

title: AC-42: the 'release waits for the settlement delay' test still passes when the delay is forced to 0
requirement: AC-42 (release waits for terminal + cumulative equality + delay + repeat scan); NG-HIST-002 settlement policy
failure_scenario: Suppose the engine passes the wrong value to evaluate_terminal_release at engine.py:1364-1373, for example 0 or another field instead of config.settlement_delay_s. A leg is then released as soon as two scans complete. Two effects follow: an execution published by the venue shortly after the terminal row is not seen before the cell is reused, and the settlement_delay_s config value has no effect. No engine test fails.
suggested_fix: Use a settlement_delay_s larger than the time two scans take (for example 20 s with poll 5 s). Record the tick at which the leg or cycle is released, not the clock after run_until, and assert release_time - first_terminal_seen >= delay and that it was not released one tick earlier.

title: AC-55: the disk-full test never reaches the intent, cancel-intent or dispatch-mark writes it claims to prove
requirement: AC-55 / NG-DB-004 (neither submit nor cancel is sent if its intent/reservation cannot be durably written)
failure_scenario: Suppose _submit or _dispatch_cancels (engine.py:1783-1953) catches a PersistenceError from the intent, cancel-intent or mark_dispatching transaction and calls the transport anyway, i.e. sends an order without a committed intent. test_ac55 still passes: under disk-full the tick aborts earlier and never gets to those writes.
suggested_fix: Inject the failure exactly at the side-effect writes. Use FaultHooks.fail_statement on the outbox/intent INSERT, or fail_commit armed right before the intent or mark_dispatching commit, while history and account writes still succeed. Assert that the fake records no submit or cancel and that state is DEGRADED with PERSISTENCE_FAILURE.

title: AC-16/17/21: the 'reservation kept' assertions pass even when the UNKNOWN leg is dropped from the risk endpoints; AC-17's check can never fail
requirement: AC-16/AC-17 (until proof, the reservation and UNKNOWN are kept); AC-21 (order and full remainder stay reserved); NG-RISK-002
failure_scenario: Suppose SUBMIT_UNKNOWN or CANCEL_UNKNOWN legs stopped counting in P_max/P_min. The router could then over-commit net exposure by the unknown order's remainder, and the named AC tests still pass. With that change applied, P_max drops from 40 to 30 in all three scenarios and each assertion still holds.
suggested_fix: Assert the exact value, e.g. endpoints.P_max == P + the sum of all non-final BUY remainders including the unknown leg (or compare with and without it). For AC-21 also check that the slot/reservation accounting still counts the order.

title: Section 11 / NG-UI-002 honest states: RECONCILING and STOPPING are never asserted, the 'honest' test has a check that cannot fail, and CLI status omits cursor progress
requirement: Section 11 (CLI status shows freshness/history lag/cursor progress...); NG-UI-002 (RECONCILING/STOPPING shown, no optimistic NORMAL); NG-HIST-003 (restart stays RECONCILING between ticks)
failure_scenario: If the engine reported PAUSED/DEGRADED during a multi-tick startup walk, or STOP_UNCERTAIN instead of STOPPING during a normal drain, no test would fail. A probe shows the current code does report RECONCILING,RECONCILING,NORMAL after a restart and STOPPING during a drain, but nothing asserts it. Separately, during a long RECONCILING walk the CLI status gives the operator no cursor/page progress. Snapshot summary.history has trades_cursor, orders_cursor, pages_read and progress, but format_status (snapshot.py:288-290) prints only complete/reason/lag/last_full_scan/weight.
suggested_fix: After restart, assert RECONCILING on the ticks before the first complete walk (with max_scan_pages_per_tick=1 and more than 100 inactive rows), and STOPPING while a stop drains. Print cursor/pages progress in format_status and assert it in the CLI test.

title: resolve_unknown_submit accepts 'not landed' on an active list and history walk from before the dispatch, so a new CID goes out while the original order is live
requirement: NG-HIST-001, NG-DB-005, AC-56, AC-16/17 (handoff: active-list absence is not proof; no new CID after a timeout)
failure_scenario: A submit times out (TransportOutcome.UNKNOWN) but lands on the venue, and the venue's active list lags by a few seconds. About 2 s later the operator sends baseline_audit {action: resolve_unknown_submit, cid}. The engine checks self.history_complete, which is true from a walk that finished before the dispatch. It then checks that the CID is absent from self.active_rows, which was fetched before the dispatch (or is None after a failed poll, which passes as an empty list). It does not check freshness, a walk started after intent_ms, or the settlement delay. The leg becomes REJECTED_ZERO_FILL, _retry_only() allows a new revision, and a second 10 LIT BUY with a new CID is placed for the same cell. Only on a later poll is the old order seen 'final but still active' (RISK_BLOCKED). By then the cell has double exposure.
suggested_fix: Accept the resolution only when all of these hold: an active list fetched successfully after the outbox dispatched_at_ms and within freshness; at least settlement_scans complete walks that started after dispatched_at_ms + settlement_delay (the same predicate as terminal release); no pending WS signal for that CID. Otherwise return EVIDENCE_EXISTS_OR_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE.

title: The launcher's automatic START on every process start clears a durable STOP / STOP_UNCERTAIN and resumes trading
requirement: NG-OPS-003, AC-36 (restart continues reconciliation; STOP_UNCERTAIN is not a success), NG-UI-003
failure_scenario: The operator stops the grid (web STOP, or Hummingbot stop leading to drain_neutral_executors), and one cancel stays unknown, giving STOP_UNCERTAIN. The drain can also exceed STOP_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S=90 s before stop_uncertain_after_s=120 s, so the durable state is still STOPPING. After any process restart, NeutralGridExecutor.on_start enqueues START with key launcher-start-<executor config id>. That id is random for every new ExecutorConfigBase, so the key is never a duplicate. START resets stop_requested_ms, stop_outcome and stop_reason to None. The drain is abandoned, the state becomes NORMAL, and new entries are submitted while the order with the uncertain cancel is still live. The launcher's log line says '(STOP_UNCERTAIN) will be reconciled on the next start', which is not what happens.
suggested_fix: Do not let an automatic launcher START override a durable stop: reject START while stop_requested_ms is set, or while stop_outcome is STOP_UNCERTAIN, unless an explicit operator command carries the idempotency key and expected revision. Make the drain timeout at least stop_uncertain_after_s, or log the real durable outcome.

title: A CID collision latches FREEZE_CID forever and blocks every TP; no audited recovery path exists
requirement: NG-RISK-003 (manual orders must not drop TP obligations), NG-OPS-001, AC-43 (fail closed without dead-locking obligations)
failure_scenario: A manual or foreign order on the account uses the client id that the store would allocate next. It is seen in active orders and recorded in foreign_cids. The next TP intent raises CidCollisionError, and the engine sets meta.freezes['CID_ALLOCATION']. That freeze is in _FREEZES_BLOCKING_TP, so no TP obligation of any cell is dispatched again. Nothing clears it: AUDIT_ACTIONS has no action for it, _cmd_reconcile never pops FREEZE_CID, and store.retire_cid (the recovery the store documents) is never called by the engine. Exits stay blocked until the operator edits the SQLite engine_kv by hand.
suggested_fix: Add an audited action such as retire_colliding_cid that calls store.retire_cid(candidate) and pops FREEZE_CID in the same command transaction. Also, a collision with an id the engine has already recorded as foreign could retire it automatically, with an audit row.

title: The baseline audit (AC-30 rebase) absorbs an own fill that history has not delivered yet into the baseline, then counts it twice
requirement: NG-RISK-003 / AC-30 (the rebase must not hide unknown fills), NG-RISK-001/002 (P = B + buys - sells)
failure_scenario: A manual BUY of 7 causes drift, and entries are blocked pending audit. While the venue's history lags, a grid entry partially fills 4. The position shows 11 at once; the trade is not yet in history. The engine has a pending WS trade signal (history_lag_s = 6 s) and venue != P. The audit is still accepted because history is 'complete and fresh', the position is fresh, and the filled entry is still LIVE, so it is not 'unresolved'. new_baseline = 11 - 0 + 0 = 11 instead of 7. When the fill reaches history, the ledger gives P = 15 against a venue position of 11. The engine reports NORMAL for the next 30 s (position_gap_grace_s), then POSITION_UNRECONCILED, and it needs a second audit. The durable audit trail records a wrong effective baseline.
suggested_fix: Reject the audit while any WS trade signal is pending, while history lag is above 0, or while an owned LIVE or partially filled order has executions not proven by a complete walk that started after the position read. Require a position fetched after the last history commit, using real read timestamps.

title: When a pre-send check fails (e.g. the runtime tick changes), the engine allocates a new CID and intent every tick, with no visible blocker and state NORMAL
requirement: NG-DB-005 (a new revision only after config/rules are fixed), AC-34 (an impossible TP must be a visible blocker), AC-14, NG-UI-002 (truthful state)
failure_scenario: Trading rules refresh with a tick size under which the fixed TP price is no longer a tick multiple. Each tick _submit allocates a new durable CID, commits the intent and reservation, and only then runs _pre_send_blocker. That returns PRICE_NOT_ON_TICK, the intent is recorded NOT_SENT (REJECTED_UNSENT), and the next tick repeats with another CID and revision, up to max_submits_per_tick. The TP obligation is never placed. cell_blockers stays empty and engine state stays NORMAL, so neither the operator nor the UI sees that the exit is blocked, while the cid_map, legs and outbox grow without bound.
suggested_fix: Run _pre_send_blocker (tick alignment, qty and order-type checks against current rules) in planning, before CID allocation. Record the result as a cell or TP blocker with queue age, and do not create a new revision until the rules or config change.

title: The stop outcome reports STOPPED (no inventory) when the venue position is unknown, even though the engine's own baseline is non-zero
requirement: NG-OPS-003 / AC-35 (STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY), NG-UI-002 (no optimistic or fake STOP)
failure_scenario: The grid was bootstrapped with B=330 and a STOP is draining. The process restarts and the account endpoint is unavailable, so self.position is None. Once every own leg is settled and history is complete, _finish_stop computes inventory only from cycle E/X/dust and 'position is not None and position != 0'. The durable outcome is STOPPED although the account holds 330 LIT (the engine's effective_baseline) and the position was never observed.
suggested_fix: Treat a non-zero effective_baseline as inventory, and do not finalise STOPPED or STOPPED_WITH_INVENTORY while the position is unknown or stale. Keep STOPPING, or use STOP_UNCERTAIN after the timeout.

title: The drift guard compares position and history using the same tick timestamp, so a position read before the history walk counts as 'not older'
requirement: NG-RISK-003 / NG-DB-003 (drift must be real; no false manual reconcile), AC-30
failure_scenario: Within one tick, _refresh_account reads the position and sets position_at = now (the tick start). The history walk then commits an own fill that landed after that read and sets last_history_commit_at to the same now. The guard `position_at < last_history_commit_at` is false, so the stale position is compared with the ledger. With no SELL remainders covering the fill, venue = P - f falls below P_min, and a durable 'position drift' manual reconcile is written. Entries stay RISK_BLOCKED until an operator baseline audit, which then also runs on a pre-history position (see the baseline-audit finding).
suggested_fix: Stamp position_at and the history commit with the real clock at the moment each read or commit completes, or skip the drift comparison when a history batch committed after the position fetch started.

title: The CLI status omits history cursor progress that section 11 requires
requirement: Spec section 11 Operator status ('freshness/history lag/cursor progress')
failure_scenario: During a multi-tick restart walk (RECONCILING) the operator runs `status`. The output shows history complete/reason/lag/last_full_scan/weight but no cursor or high-water, pages read or boundary progress. The snapshot has summary.history.trades_cursor, orders_cursor, pages_read and progress, but format_status drops them, so the CLI cannot show whether reconciliation is advancing, unlike the UI.
suggested_fix: Add the trades/orders high-water (or its timestamp), pages read and the scanner progress (resumable, boundary reached) to the history line of format_status.

title: The Robinhood launcher treats the 1000 LIT caps as a hard ceiling instead of a default
requirement: NG-ARCH-003 (max_abs_net_position/max_gross_position are a positive user limit, not a product ceiling), NG-RISK-002 (not a hardcoded maximum), NG-ARCH-001 (launcher pins cap defaults)
failure_scenario: An operator configures max_abs_net_position: 1500 (a positive user limit that the spec explicitly allows). validate_profile refuses the start with 'exceeds the Robinhood profile cap 1000 LIT' and forces enabled=False, making 1000 LIT a product ceiling.
suggested_fix: Use DEFAULT_CAPS only as defaults or example values. Validate that the caps are positive and finite, and leave the effective limit to the operator (optionally with a warning when it differs from the profile).
